reply_text:
I found one dated AI prediction from Huang in 2022 that is new, plus two shipping dates already in your files. Two more automotive dates are borderline. None of them are Huang's words in a transcript. They come from Nvidia's own wrap-up posts on its GTC keynotes, so each is marked coverage_only.

- **The one new candidate, and it's borderline.** At the March 22, 2022 GTC keynote, Nvidia's blog quotes Huang as saying Nvidia "will strive for yet another million-X in the next decade". He means a millionfold speed-up in AI computing. It is stated as a goal ("strive"), and it is about compute speed, which sits close to the chips rule. Keep or drop it on that basis.
- **Already recorded.** The same blog post says Hyperion 8 ships in Mercedes-Benz cars from 2024 and Jaguar Land Rover cars from 2025. That is the post's summary of what Huang said, not a direct quote of him.
- **Two borderline automotive dates.** The blog also says Hyperion 9 would ship from 2026 and that BYD would use Drive Orin in cars from the first half of 2023. Both are in the writer's words after "Huang announced", and both lean toward product or customer plans. Nvidia's September 2022 keynote post says the new Thor chip replaced Atlan on its Drive roadmap. Atlan was the chip inside Hyperion 9, so that 2026 date was effectively withdrawn.
- **Nothing else qualifies.** I found no 2022 statement on when AGI or superintelligence arrives. Both 2022 Stratechery interviews (March and September) are forward-looking but carry no dates, and the March one cut off partway through the version I could open. A search snippet suggests that interview includes an exchange about "AI is always 10 years away", but I couldn't open that part, so I haven't quoted it. The September 2022 dates I saw (Grace Hopper in the first half of 2023, H100 cloud instances "next year") are chip launches, so they stay out.
